attempted_axis: de-fakematch pass over all 37 census raw-cast sites in src/game/anim/action.c: resolve every *(TYPE*)(ptr + N) site to offsetof()-on-the-same-raw-pointer against a GC-verified struct field (include/game/enemy.h Enemy/animinfo, include/game/player.h Player, include/game/leveldata.h level_data), never introducing a typed intermediate pointer or repeated inline cast; introduce a file-local ATREESEQ view struct only where no header covers the field (InitActions' 48-byte sequence-table stride). Gated per-region on defake_gate.py baseline/check (fndiff real+ops/--clean, not fuzzy) with a full ninja+doldiff gate at the end. Both DoEnemyAction (REGISTER_ONLY parked residual) and DoPlayerAction (extensively documented whole-function register-pressure fragility, 'ANY touch' cascades on several axes per attempt.doplayeraction-mwcc-shape-closure.20260830.v1) made this pass higher-risk than a typical TU; the offsetof-only technique was chosen specifically because it changes no pointer type and no live web, and was verified not to disturb either function's residual.

attributes.converted: 36 of 37 census sites resolved to named forms, ALL byte-identical / zero regression, verified via defake_gate.py check (GATE OK) plus fndiff --count and --clean on each touched function before/after: DoEnemyAction (482/482 insns, real 2, lines 28 - unchanged, including the pre-existing PARKED 204(r27) vs 204(r3) register tie which is untouched since these 3 sites are far from that web) - e70+0x34/+0x10 -> offsetof(animinfo, repeat)/offsetof(animinfo, numframes) (e70 == &enemy->atree.animinfo, confirmed structurally: animinfo's animseq/numframes/repeat/stage offsets 0x0E/0x10/0x34/0x36 all matched the pre-existing bare-hex literals exactly), gCurLevel+0xC0 -> offsetof(level_data, ene_mrate) (also an exact literal match, cross-confirming the field id against the already GC-verified leveldata.h entry). DoPlayerAction (1765/1765 insns, real 1852, lines 2048 - unchanged, all 33 converted sites): 10x weaphold_node (void* @0x6E0), 3x vibe_timer (s16 @0x200), 3x vibe_timer2 (s16 @0x202), 9x hud_flags (s16 @0x964), 2x grab_flags (s16 @0x962), 1x throw_str (s16 @0x958) - all resolved via offsetof(Player, field) on the untyped `(u8*)p` pointer, using Player fields player.h already documents as GC-verified via player.c's own target asm ([player.c] tag); 4x animinfo fields (stage/repeat/animseq/numframes) on the `atree` local (== &player's own embedded atree.animinfo at player+0x80, same structural match method as DoEnemyAction's e70). Full ninja green at the end; build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK; project progress numbers unchanged (97.82% fuzzy/58.15% matched/26.09% linked) as expected for a byte-identical pass; git diff --check passes; only action.c touched.
attributes.law_screen: offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web: the PRIMARY and only law actually needed - every one of the 36 converted sites is a bare-hex-to-offsetof re-spelling on the function's PRE-EXISTING raw pointer (e, e70, ef, p, atree, gCurLevel, atree->seqs), with zero pointer-type changes and zero new typed lvalues anywhere; this matches the law's stated form exactly and its 'near-guaranteed neutral' prediction held for all 36 sites including inside DoPlayerAction's documented extreme-register-pressure function. declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast / multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing v2: screened, deliberately NOT applied - both govern introducing a typed alias or typed struct member access, which this pass avoided entirely by design given DoPlayerAction's recorded fragility; not needed since offsetof alone closed all resolvable sites. offsetof-fused-immediate-counter: screened; its 'walked loop reaching a field several levels deep' scenario doesn't apply here (no walked accumulator pointers in this TU - e/p/atree are all plain function-parameter-derived pointers, not `+=`-walked), but the same underlying mechanism (keep the raw pointer, single additive offsetof expression) is what this pass used throughout, so it's the closest analogue and is cited for that reason. offsetof-overturns-typed-alias-caps: screened; not directly applicable (this TU had no PRIOR cap on these specific sites to overturn), but its evidence that offsetof-on-raw-pointer scales safely to 50+ sites without bisection directly motivated converting all 33 DoPlayerAction sites in one batch rather than pre-emptively splitting them. large-fn-batch-fuzzy-can-mask-subfield-regression: screened; DoPlayerAction (1765 insns) is under the ~4000-insn fuzzy-arbitration threshold, but fndiff --count's real/insn-parity was checked explicitly anyway per this law's general caution, and held exactly steady (1852/1765/1765 before and after the full 33-site batch). lwzu-idiom-web-retention / scalar-read-write-lfsu-mixed-form: screened; no lwzu-fusable prologue and no adjacent same-address read-then-write pair among any of the 37 sites (DoEnemyAction's `*(s16*)(e70+off)=interruptible` is a standalone write with no adjacent read of the same address; the vibe_timer/vibe_timer2 pairs at case 1/3 are two DIFFERENT fields, not a read-write pair on one field) - not applicable. pointer-walk-array-index-regression / recomputed-index-array-form-safe: screened; none of the converted bases are walked (`+=`-accumulated) or freshly-recomputed-per-iteration array indices - not applicable, no loop is involved in any of the 37 sites. walked-base-symbol-identity: screened; gCurLevel is a single extern pointer here (not two overlapping named globals), and the level_data field chosen (ene_mrate) was cross-confirmed by the pre-existing bare-hex literal (0xC0) matching leveldata.h's already-GC-verified entry exactly, not by guessing between two symbols - not applicable but the exact-literal-match cross-check served the same verification purpose this law calls for.
attributes.left_raw: 1 site: DoPlayerAction's *(s16*)((u8*)p + 0x956) (line ~1251, action band 0x73/collision-recovery check `& 4`). 0x956 falls inside player.h's pad_0956[2] gap (between speak_timer@0x954 and throw_str@0x958) with no GC-verified name; `gdlmem.py struct Player --offset 0x956` resolved to an unrelated Xbox struct (`playermodelinfo`, a false-positive name match on the query string, offset reported 'outside recorded layout'). Cross-checked against every other TU that touches this exact byte offset via grep for '0x956' across src/: pmotion.c (2 sites) and player.c (1 site) all access it through the project's raw PF(p, 0x956, s16) macro too, with no resolved name anywhere in the tree - confirms this is a genuinely unresolved GC-only field shared/consistent across TUs, not an oversight local to action.c. Left raw per the 'never invent names' rule; a future pass that resolves PF(p,0x956,*) project-wide (likely via pmotion.c/player.c target-asm bit semantics, since it's tested with masks 2/4/0x10/128) should also close this action.c site.
